items.student_text: A puck moves east at constant speed while the net force is zero. What will its velocity do next if the net force remains zero?
items.student_html: A puck moves east at constant speed while the net force is zero. What will its velocity do next if the net force remains zero?
items.solution_text: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no change in velocity.
items.solution_html: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no change in velocity.

items.student_text: Which situation is consistent with zero net force?
items.student_html: Which situation is consistent with zero net force?

choices.text: A bicycle turning at constant speed
A book resting on a level desk
A ball slowing as it rolls

answer.text: A book resting on a level desk

items.solution_text: A resting book can have support and weight forces that cancel, giving zero net force.
items.solution_html: A resting book can have support and weight forces that cancel, giving zero net force.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain that inertia is a property of matter, not a force.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.2: Newton’s First Law, inertia, zero-net-force distinction, support force/weight; Physics Framework: physical-situation force reasoning.
items.student_text: A student says, “A massive cart has a stronger inertia force pushing it forward.” Correct the statement.
items.student_html: A student says, “A massive cart has a stronger inertia force pushing it forward.” Correct the statement.
items.answer: Inertia is not a force; it is a property of matter associated with resistance to a change in velocity.
items.solution_text: A force is an interaction. Inertia describes how matter resists changes in motion.
items.solution_html: A force is an interaction. Inertia describes how matter resists changes in motion.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain that inertia is a property of matter, not a force.
items.evidence_job: Recognize inertia as a property of matter in context.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.2: Newton’s First Law, inertia, zero-net-force distinction, support force/weight; Physics Framework: physical-situation force reasoning.

choices.text: It is a forward force carried by moving objects.
It is a property of matter that resists changes in velocity.
It exists only when an object is moving.
It is the same as net force.

answer.text: It is a property of matter that resists changes in velocity.

items.solution_text: Inertia is a property, not a force, and matter has it whether at rest or moving.
items.solution_html: Inertia is a property, not a force, and matter has it whether at rest or moving.

items.student_text: Diagram: 22 N support ↑ [box] 22 N weight ↓. The box is motionless. Explain why this is “zero net force,” not “no forces.”
items.student_html: Diagram: 22 N support ↑ [box] 22 N weight ↓. The box is motionless. Explain why this is “zero net force,” not “no forces.”
items.answer: Two real forces act but cancel, so their vector sum is zero.
items.solution_text: Support and weight are both present. Equal opposite vectors add to zero.
items.solution_html: Support and weight are both present. Equal opposite vectors add to zero.
